independent_reasoning: For a prescription drug delivered to a location other than a pharmacy, Massachusetts law permits the counseling-offer requirement to be satisfied through access to a toll-free telephone service that facilitates communication with the pharmacist, but the toll-free service number must also be printed on a label affixed to each container of the prescription drug. Therefore choice A is the single best answer; placement only on an outer package or receipt, post-delivery electronic transmission, or substitution of an ordinary local number does not satisfy the stated requirement.

official_authority_consulted.relevance: Current statutory text expressly requires the toll-free telephone service number to be printed on a label affixed to each container of a prescription drug when the prescription is delivered away from the pharmacy.
